title: Did the economy break Trump? Enten unpacks the numbers
summary: CNN segment on the hot September CPI and PPI: Enten on Trump's collapsed economic approval, Daniel Dale debunking the 1.7% and 19% inflation claims and noting inflation is higher than when Trump took office.

assertions.quote: We have not had anywhere close to 1.7 inflation in the last 3 months. We had 3.4% in July, 3.4% in August, up to 3.7%
Biden era inflation did peak at 9.1% uh June 2022
even that 9.1% 40-year peak was nowhere close to the all-time high. The all-time high is 23.7% in 1920.
inflation was lower when President Trump took office than it is now
he said that all your prices are falling fast. Well, the vast majority of prices continue to increase.

verdicts.note: The September 2026 CPI rose 0.6% on the month with most categories up; only food at home dipped.

In September 2026 the all-items index rose 0.6% and core 0.3%, with recreation, used cars, education, airline fares, medical care and apparel all up; BLS says communication was among the small number of major indexes that decreased.

assertions.quote: Uh that is not even close to true. Average consumer prices according to the CPI are 5.4% higher.

verdicts.note: The CPI level rose about 5% between January 2025 and September 2026.
The NSA CPI-U rose from 317.671 in January 2025 to 336.94 in September 2026, a 6.1% increase in the average price level.

assertions.quote: the producer price index is up 1.3% from September and more than 6% from a year ago
It hasn't been as low as three since the Iran war started in March.

verdicts.note: CPI ran 3.3-3.7% from spring through September 2026 after 3.0% in January 2025 and lower readings in 2025.

Headline 12-month CPI was 3.3% in March 2026, 3.8% April, 4.2% May, 3.5% June, 3.4% July, 3.4% August and 3.7% September, every month since the March 2026 gasoline jump (+24.9%) that marks the conflict's onset in the price data; the war's start date itself is not in these documents.
